title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of the Regulation on Disciplinary Punishment of Court Personnel
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Reply on Issues Concerning the Application of the Disciplinary Punishment Regulations for Personnel of the People's Court

Fa [2010] No. 148

Hunan High People's Court:

Your Request for Instructions on Several Issues Concerning How to Apply the Disciplinary Punishment Regulations for Personnel of the People's Court has been received. Upon review, we reply as follows:

1. The Disciplinary Punishment Regulations for Personnel of the People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the Regulations) do not apply retroactively. For cases in which a disciplinary decision was made before the promulgation of the Regulations, if a review or reconsideration is required, the provisions in effect at the time shall apply. For cases in which no disciplinary decision has yet been made, if the provisions in effect at the time of the conduct did not consider it a disciplinary violation, but the Regulations do, the provisions in effect at the time shall apply. If the provisions in effect at the time of the conduct considered it a disciplinary violation, those provisions shall apply; however, if the Regulations do not consider it a disciplinary violation or the punishment is lighter, the Regulations shall apply.

2. After retirement, if a person working in a people's court should have their benefits reduced or cancelled due to disciplinary or legal violations, the supervisory department of the court where the person originally worked shall, with reference to the Ministry of Supervision's Notice on Several Issues Concerning the Pursuit of Administrative Disciplinary Responsibility for Retired Civil Servants Who Have Committed Errors (Jian Fa [2001] No. 3) and the Ministry of Supervision's Reply on How to Deduct Pensions in Pursuing Administrative Disciplinary Responsibility for Retired Civil Servants Who Have Committed Errors (Jian Fa Fu [2004] No. 1), submit supervisory recommendations to the organizational and personnel department, and that department shall handle the relevant procedures.

3. After retirement, if a court leading cadre who was originally under the supervision of the supervisory department of a higher court needs to have their benefits reduced or cancelled due to disciplinary or legal violations, the higher court shall submit supervisory recommendations to the court where the retired person originally worked, and the organizational and personnel department of that court shall handle the relevant procedures.

This is our reply.

April 6, 2010
